_note: Sister IEEE societies/councils a Signal Processing Society chapter most often co-hosts with. `overlap` lists the shared technical ground, `joint_formats` lists event shapes that have precedent, `pitch_angle` is the argument that usually wins their chapter over.

societies.name: IEEE Communications Society
societies.pitch_angle: ISAC (integrated sensing and communication) is the live shared frontier - both societies claim it, so a joint event avoids a turf argument and doubles the speaker pool.

societies.name: IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society
societies.pitch_angle: Biomedical signal processing needs clinicians in the room. EMBS brings the clinical partner and the dataset; SPS brings the methods. Also the easiest joint event to attract non-engineering attendees to.

societies.name: IEEE Computational Intelligence Society
societies.pitch_angle: Nearly every modern SPS paper uses learned models. CIS chapters usually have the ML speaker bench; SPS supplies the application domains and the data.

societies.name: IEEE Circuits and Systems Society
societies.pitch_angle: Implementation-flavoured events. CAS covers the silicon, SPS the algorithm. Strong with electronics-heavy student bodies and easy to run as a hardware lab.

societies.name: IEEE Computer Society
societies.pitch_angle: Largest student membership on most campuses - partner with them when the goal is turnout rather than technical depth.

societies.name: IEEE Robotics and Automation Society
societies.pitch_angle: Perception is signal processing wearing a robot. Highly demo-able, which makes it the best joint format for public-facing or open-day events.

societies.name: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Society
societies.pitch_angle: GRSS runs generous open-data challenges and has strong India-region activity through ISRO-adjacent collaborations.

societies.name: IEEE Information Theory Society
societies.pitch_angle: Theory-heavy, small but high-prestige audiences. Best as a distinguished lecture rather than a mass event.

societies.name: IEEE Sensors Council
societies.pitch_angle: Councils are often looking for chapters to co-run activities and can be easier to get sponsorship from than large societies.

societies.name: IEEE Women in Engineering
societies.pitch_angle: Co-hosting with WIE materially improves reporting metrics and is viewed favourably in Section awards. Pair a technical SPS talk with a WIE career panel in one evening.

societies.name: IEEE Young Professionals
societies.pitch_angle: YP brings recent-graduate speakers who are cheap to host and relatable to students. Good bridge to industry sponsorship.

societies.name: IEEE Power & Energy Society
societies.pitch_angle: Underused pairing. Grid fault detection is a genuine signal processing problem and PES chapters are usually well funded.
